outcomes.text: Understand short recordings about everyday needs, including shopping transactions, directions and instructions.
Understand factual information and ideas about familiar topics from announcements, messages, news, interviews and dialogues.
Understand descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions in simple spoken texts.
Identify main points, specific information and details in recordings about everyday topics.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable spoken texts.
Infer the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from listening context.
Understand short, simple texts such as public signs, notices and instructions.
Understand authentic texts about familiar topics, including articles, emails, blogs and letters.
Understand descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions in simple written texts.
Identify main points, specific information and details in predictable written texts.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable written texts.
Infer the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from reading context.
Take part in short social exchanges and communicate about familiar topics to meet simple needs.
Participate in spontaneous conversations about personal interests and everyday life.
Describe past events and experiences, discuss hopes and ambitions, and briefly justify opinions and plans.
Communicate reasonably accurately using varied structures, tenses and relevant vocabulary.
Connect shorter points into a sequence using simple linking words.
Use suitable strategies to keep conversations going.
Use pronunciation and intonation features to communicate meaning and attitude.
Complete forms by providing simple personal details.
Write simple factual information using everyday vocabulary and expressions.
Write linked phrases and sentences about personal life, surroundings and everyday topics.
Write connected texts about familiar subjects, including plans, preferences, family, education, work and travel.
Describe past events and experiences, opinions, hopes and ambitions, with brief supporting reasons.
Communicate reasonably accurately using varied structures, tenses, time frames and relevant vocabulary.
Link shorter written points into a connected sequence using simple connectors.
Use Japanese time expressions for telling the time, days, months and seasons.
Give times, dates including years, and durations such as weeks, months and years.
Use vocabulary for meals, fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, seafood, snacks, drinks, cutlery and utensils.
Use vocabulary related to travel and transport.
Use polite and plain forms of です in non-past, negative, past and past-negative statements, including で to link clauses.
Use polite and plain verb forms in non-past, negative, past and past-negative contexts.
Express suggestions and invitations using ましょうか and ませんか.
Express wanting or not wanting to do something in present and past contexts.
Express doing one action while doing another, going or coming for a purpose, and ease or difficulty.
Describe beginning, continuing or finishing an action.
Explain how to do something, express excess, and give polite commands.
Give commands and describe actions occurring in sequence.
Express an action performed before another, continuous action and present states.
Give or refuse permission and describe trying something.
Talk about past experience and actions completed before another action.
Describe non-sequential actions, give advice, and express possibility or uncertainty.
Express actions before another event, intentions, plans, purposes and circumstances using dictionary forms.
Express ability and preferences, dislikes, skill, lack of skill or importance concerning activities.
Express possibility or probability with dictionary-form structures.
Give negative commands and negative advice.
Express obligations and things that are not necessary.
Express possibility or probability with negative-form structures.
Use plain forms before と思います, と言います and と書きます.
Use を to mark objects and places passed through during movement.
Use か, から, が, し, しか and で for alternatives, origins, subjects, reasons, limitation and locations or means.
Use と, に, ね, の and ので for accompaniment, destinations, times, indirect objects, possession and reasons.
Use は, へ, まで, も and や to mark topics, destinations, limits, additions and examples.
Use でも, よ and わ to offer choices or add sentence-final emphasis.
Use い-adjectives in polite and plain non-past, negative, past and past-negative forms.
Use both adjective types before nouns, at sentence endings and to link clauses.
Use adjectives adverbially and before する or なる.
Use plain adjective forms before expressions meaning think, say or write.
Express excess, possibility and probability with adjectives.
Use noun-plus-の expressions to indicate before or after, time, position and purpose.
Use ある before a noun to mean a particular or unspecified person, day or thing.
Make comparative statements and ask which of two things has a greater quality.
Form superlative statements and questions within a group.
Use suffixes for forms of address, nationality, shops, plurals, languages and rooms.
Form questions with か, question words, alternative choices and common question-word particles.
Use counters for people, objects, money, occurrences, floors, drinks, age, stays and degrees.
Use 目 and ずつ after general numbers or counters.
Use demonstratives for objects, locations, directions and types of thing at varying distances.
